title: Best AI Agent Templates to Run Today Without Code
summary: AI agent templates help you build automated workflows without coding. Compare Zapier and alternatives to find the right fit for your team.
body_markdown:
## 3. Activepieces: best for open-source agent workflows


### Why it suits you


If you expect to rebuild credentials and knowledge sources anyway, Activepieces suits you. Its core is MIT-licensed and its 740 integrations sit in the open repo, so you can read every step you'll edit and **the fix-after-copy cost is visible** before you commit.


It's an open-source automation builder with AI steps, aimed at teams past the pilot stage who want to measure editing time per template.


Pick Zapier instead if your apps are long-tail and you want the widest app coverage. Pick Lindy if you'd rather configure a prebuilt agent than edit a flow.


### The template in practice


When a new email lands in[Gmail](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/gmail) , an AI step classifies it as urgent, routine or noise. A[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) message alerts the owner of urgent items, and[Google Sheets](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-sheets) logs every classification.


The free plan on Activepieces Cloud costs $0 with no card needed, and it includes unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, so you can[run this flow](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fbest-ai-agent-templates-to-run-today-without-code) before paying anything.


Open the builder and you see what you'll actually touch.


It has a Schedule trigger set to Every Hour, an integration picker listing Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel 365, AITable and Retable with actions such as Insert Row and Find Rows, and a test run returning sample data.


That's your edit list, and the logging step is where the sheet connection gets swapped.


Once that connection exists, the edit is not repeated for agents: the same Google Sheets integration that runs as a step here is also a tool on[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) ' per-project MCP server, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent you wrote can call it.


The packages/integrations/community directory of the open source repo holds 740 integrations, each written once as an action, and the Integrations Framework and MCP Server documentation describe that same action as the one a flow runs and the one the MCP server exposes as a tool.


### Cost and trade-offs


Checked 2026-10-15:[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) lists Free at $0 a month, Plus at $20 and Team at $200, meaning users can start without paying to evaluate it. The free tier lets you run the triage flow before spending anything.


The Team step is ten times Plus, so move up only when your edit and run volume justifies it.


You can see and change every step, the open-source base gives you a way out of lock-in, and the free tier makes a measured pilot cheap.


Before it runs, a template still needs your credentials and your classification rules. Expect to tune the AI step's prompt against real mail before trusting it, and expect a smaller pool of ready-made agent flows than the biggest catalogs offer.
